The metadata shows only ordinary document properties and an old template date, which is not something I would flag under Rule 4.4(b). From a Buyer perspective, the immediate leverage points are price, closing certainty, and broader Seller protection through reps and confidentiality exceptions. receiver.requested_changes: 1) Price: reduce the purchase price materially from USD 45,000,000. If Seller will not move on headline price, Buyer will need an earnout, escrow/holdback, or a working-capital/net debt adjustment to preserve economics. 2) Closing: extend the outside date beyond 45 days and make closing conditional on delivery of definitive, objective deliverables rather than open-ended ‘good-faith completion.’ Buyer should not be forced to close if Seller items remain incomplete. 3) Representations: replace ‘to the best of its knowledge’ and ‘in all material respects’ with a fuller, more seller-specific rep package, including accuracy of financial statements without materiality qualifiers where appropriate, and add standard reps on authority, title to shares, no undisclosed liabilities, compliance with law, taxes, litigation, and absence of MAE. 4) Confidentiality: expand permitted disclosures to Buyer’s financing sources, advisers, affiliates, regulatory authorities, and to the extent required for ordinary-course integration/planning, subject to customary confidentiality obligations where appropriate. 5) General: add a survival period for reps and a clear indemnity regime so the Buyer has meaningful post-closing recourse.
receiver.message_back: Thank you for the draft. We’ve reviewed it and have a few points to move this toward signing efficiently, but we do need better buyer protection on the economics and risk allocation. In particular, the USD 45,000,000 price is too rich on current terms, and the 45-day closing timetable is too tight given the open-ended ‘good-faith’ deliverables language. We also need a fuller rep package, not just a knowledge/materiality-qualified financial statement rep, and broader confidentiality carve-outs for our advisers, financing sources, affiliates, and any required regulatory or legal disclosures. If you can circulate a revised draft addressing those items, we should be able to keep momentum.

edits.text: 2. Closing. Closing shall occur within 60 days of signing, subject only to the satisfaction or waiver of the specific closing deliverables set forth in this Agreement, each to be delivered in definitive form and in accordance with applicable law.

3. Representations. The Seller represents that, to its knowledge and in all material respects, it has the authority to enter into this Agreement; it owns the Shares free and clear of liens other than Permitted Encumbrances; the financial statements fairly present, in all material respects, the financial condition and results of operations of the Company; and, to the extent specifically stated in this Agreement, there are no undisclosed liabilities, material compliance violations, material tax deficiencies, pending or threatened litigation, or material adverse effect affecting the Company.

4. Confidentiality. The terms of this Agreement are confidential, except as required by applicable law, regulation, court order, or stock exchange rule, and except for disclosures to the parties’ respective affiliates, financing sources, legal, accounting, tax, and other professional advisers, and governmental or regulatory authorities, in each case on a need-to-know basis and subject, where practicable, to customary confidentiality obligations; provided that Buyer may also disclose such terms as reasonably necessary for ordinary-course integration, planning, and financing purposes, subject to customary confidentiality protections.

5. Survival; Indemnity. The representations and warranties shall survive for 12 months after Closing, except for fundamental representations and tax matters, which shall survive for the applicable statutory period. The Seller’s aggregate liability for indemnifiable breaches shall be capped at 10% of the Purchase Price, subject to a customary basket and de minimis threshold, and the Buyer’s sole and exclusive remedy for such breaches shall be indemnification under this Agreement, except in cases of fraud.

receiver.requested_changes: 1. Reduce purchase price from USD 45,000,000 to USD 42,500,000 (or lower, if Seller wants to keep the current risk profile). 2. Expand the Seller’s reps to include full authority, title, capitalization, no undisclosed liabilities, compliance, tax, litigation, IP, contracts, and absence of MAE, with less reliance on knowledge qualifiers and “material respects.” 3. Tighten closing to a buyer-protective conditions precedent package: all deliverables in form and substance reasonably satisfactory to Buyer, bring-down of reps at closing, no material adverse change, and no undisclosed liens or defaults. 4. Rework survival/indemnity: extend general survival to 18–24 months, longer for tax/fundamental reps; increase cap materially; require a larger basket and no de minimis for fundamental matters; and preserve equitable relief and setoff rights rather than making indemnity the sole and exclusive remedy in all cases. 5. Narrow confidentiality carve-outs so Buyer disclosures for integration, financing, and diligence are expressly permitted without overbroad “need-to-know” constraints that could impede execution.
receiver.message_back: Thanks. The revised draft moves in the right direction on mechanics, but it still leaves the Buyer carrying too much economic and post-closing risk at the current price. We’d like to come back with a more balanced package: a lower purchase price, stronger closing conditions, broader and more complete Seller reps, and a more Buyer-protective survival/indemnity regime. If Seller is prepared to meet us on those points, we should be able to keep momentum toward signing quickly.
